slots.body:

The 2-year is 4.9%; the 2s10s spread is 0.27 percentage points—short-term and long-term government borrowing costs remain close together.

slots.title: US cash session — Nov. 17, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 lost 145.08 points, closing at 7,416.59, a 1.9% decline.
The session ranged between 7,515.60 and 7,400.15.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 626.51 points to 24,509.76, down 2.5%, with an intraday span from 24,882.04 down to 24,460.28.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished at 51,608.17, down 739.38 points or 1.4%.
The Russell 2000 closed at 2,742.94, off 1.7%.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 3.61 points to 22.91, an 18.7% move from the prior 19.30 print, tagging the session high in the feed.

Headlines in the injected set tied global equity weakness to U.S. Commerce Department action on chip shipments and broader concern around the AI trade; Asian benchmarks were already softer, with the Nikkei 225 down 1.1% at 58,987.41.

Semiconductor and AI-adjacent megacaps led the U.S. weakness:
- $NVDA -4.1% to 156.14
- $ASML -5.9% to 1,406.79
- $ORCL -5.0% to 119.05

$NVDA remained on the earnings calendar with estimates of 2.48 EPS and about $109.0B revenue.

- $GOOGL -4.1% to 283.72
- $GOOG -3.8% to 281.26
- $AMZN -3.3% to 257.75
- $META -2.4% to 626.41

Sector averages on Nasdaq were broadly negative; Communication Services averaged about -2.6%, Energy about -2.1%, Healthcare about -1.8%, Consumer Cyclical about -1.7%, and Technology about -1.2%.
Real Estate was roughly flat at 0.0% in the snapshot; Consumer Defensive was also near flat.

Financial megacaps participated in the drag:

- $V +0.2% to 426.46
- $MA +0.1% to 661.71

- $PG +1.9% to 173.02

$WMT edged up 0.2% to 128.41.

The economic calendar listed multiple October retail sales releases at 13:30 with estimates but no actuals in this payload; Atlanta Fed GDPNow for Q4 printed at 3.5%, matching the 3.5 estimate and prior in the feed.

Cross-asset reads from the injection: gold futures (GCUSD) +0.6% to 3,874.20; the oil ETF $USO proxy -3.8% to 140.03; Brent crude -0.4% to 92.03; dollar-bullish fund $UUP +0.2% to 29.56; Bitcoin -0.7% to 64,366.29.
